tasks.short: Build projections of costs and revenues per site and customer from AFAS and agency data, and advise the Controller.

today.trigger: Quarterly reforecast, a request from the Finance Director, or a large customer contract change.
steps: Export the general ledger and the open AR and AP from AFAS into Excel
Collect flex worker hours and invoices from the three agency portals
Adjust the drivers (volumes, hourly rates, CAO indexation) by hand in the forecast workbook
Write a short note on trends and risks for the Controller and FP&A
drudgery: Re-mapping AFAS exports into the forecast workbook every quarter
Downloading and matching agency invoices per site
today.time_sinks: Data collection and reconciling the agency figures with AFAS take most of the time; the analysis itself is short.

lenses.faster: A nightly pipeline already loads AFAS and agency data into a driver model, so the accountant starts from a populated forecast instead of exports.
lenses.autonomous: When the month closes in AFAS, an agent refreshes the projection and flags drivers that moved more than a set threshold.
lenses.ambitious: A rolling 13-week cash and cost forecast per site and per large customer, updated weekly instead of four times a year.
lenses.joy: No more copy-paste of exports; the time goes into asking site managers why volumes shift.
lenses.options: Three scenarios each time (peak season flex demand high, base, customer loss) with the effect on margin and cash.
lenses.altitude: The accountant owns the driver model and its assumptions log and checks the agent's output against actuals each month.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer: cash-in projection from DSO trends

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which customer contracts are about to change and which site figures the business does not trust; signing off the assumptions.
tasks.pattern_why: Several sources, exceptions in agency data and judgment on drivers; the projection should not reach management until the accountant approves it.

in_practice.trigger: Month close status set to closed in AFAS, plus quarterly reforecast date.
steps: Pull GL, AR, AP via AFAS GetConnectors and agency hours/invoices into a staging table
Recalculate driver-based projection per site in the model
Draft a variance-and-trend note with the top five movements
Accountant reviews assumptions and edits the note
Publish to the Power BI forecast page and send to Controller
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant approves assumptions and the note before publishing.
systems: Microsoft 365 Copilot or a Claude-based agent
data_needed: GL actuals per site and cost centre
in_practice.logs_to: Assumptions log on SharePoint with version per forecast run

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit exposes data through GetConnectors (REST) for extraction
Copilot in Excel can propose formulas and summarize trends in a workbook
An LLM can draft a reliable trend note from a structured variance table

risks: Agency data in inconsistent formats breaks the pipeline
Management trusts a polished projection more than its assumptions deserve
Customer data shared with an external model without a processing agreement (AVG)
research_questions: How far off were the last four quarterly forecasts, and which drivers caused the error?
Can all three agency portals deliver hours and invoices as a file or API, or only PDF?
Would FP&A accept a shared driver model owned by the accountants?

tasks.short: Check AFAS and bank data for weak controls, duplicate payments, odd supplier changes and policy breaches.

today.trigger: Annual audit preparation, a request from the Controller, or a suspicious payment noticed by a bookkeeper.
steps: Export AP, vendor master changes and payment batches from AFAS and Rabobank
Run Excel filters for duplicate invoice numbers and amounts
Spot-check approvals against the authorisation matrix
Write findings for the Controller
drudgery: Building the same duplicate and approval checks in Excel every time
Matching agency invoices against hours by hand
today.time_sinks: Checks run only once or twice a year on samples, so building the dataset dominates and coverage stays low.

lenses.faster: Rule-based tests run on the full population in minutes, so sampling and Excel filtering disappear.
lenses.autonomous: Every payment batch is screened before it goes to Rabobank: duplicate invoices, changed IBANs, approvals below the threshold, agency invoices that exceed recorded hours.
lenses.ambitious: Continuous control monitoring over 100% of transactions, with a monthly control report the external auditor can rely on.
lenses.joy: No more hunting through exports; the accountant investigates the few real hits.
lenses.options: Each hit comes with likely explanations ranked, so the accountant chooses which to follow up.
lenses.altitude: The accountant designs and tunes the control rules and thresholds and reviews false positive rates.
reach: Bookkeeper: pre-payment checks on AP batches
Controller: control framework documentation for the auditor

tasks.human_edge: Judging intent, talking to the people involved, and deciding when a finding becomes an investigation; works council and privacy rules apply when employees are named.
tasks.pattern_why: Most tests are written rules on structured data (duplicates, IBAN changes, segregation of duties); an LLM step only helps summarise hits.

in_practice.trigger: New payment batch prepared in AFAS; vendor master change; nightly run on GL.
steps: Load AP, vendor master log, payment batch and agency hours into a test database
Run the rule set and score each hit
Hold flagged payments from the Rabobank batch
Accountant reviews hits, clears or escalates
Monthly summary to Controller
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant clears or escalates each held payment; any investigation of an employee goes to the Controller and HR.
in_practice.logs_to: Control exceptions register in SharePoint list with resolution per hit

evidence.claim: MindBridge applies anomaly detection to full general ledger populations
Duplicate payment and vendor change tests are standard in data analytics tools for audit
Rules on AFAS data can be built in a few weeks with AI coding assistance

risks: Too many false positives cause people to ignore alerts
Monitoring that touches individual employees may need works council consent (WOR art. 27) and a DPIA under AVG
Holding payments late in the run delays suppliers
research_questions: How many duplicate or wrong payments were recovered in the last two years?
Does AFAS log vendor IBAN changes with user and timestamp?
Does the OR see transaction monitoring as a personnel monitoring system under art. 27?

tasks.short: Maintain site and department budgets and send monthly budget versus actual reports with explanations.

today.trigger: Month close completed in AFAS; annual budget cycle in autumn.
steps: Refresh the budget versus actual workbook from the AFAS extract
Check mappings for new cost centres and accounts
Ask budget holders by mail for explanations of large variances
Write commentary and send the pack to management
drudgery: Fixing mappings and broken links in the workbook every month
today.time_sinks: Chasing explanations and writing commentary, which often delays the pack by several days.

lenses.faster: The variance report builds itself in Power BI from the nightly extract and a first commentary is drafted, so the accountant edits instead of writes.
lenses.autonomous: On close, variances above threshold trigger a Teams question to the budget holder with the transactions behind it; answers flow into the commentary.
lenses.ambitious: Weekly flash reports per site for labour and agency costs, the largest controllable cost, instead of only monthly.
lenses.joy: No more broken Excel links or reminder mails; the accountant discusses real deviations with site managers.
lenses.options: For the budget cycle, three budget versions per site based on volume scenarios.
lenses.altitude: The accountant owns the mapping table, the thresholds and the commentary quality check.

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which explanations are credible and challenging budget holders.
tasks.pattern_why: Budget versus actual is a fixed calculation on structured data; the LLM commentary is a small step inside it.

in_practice.trigger: AFAS period closed and nightly extract refreshed.
steps: Power BI computes variances per cost centre against budget
Flag variances above threshold and list top transactions
Send Teams questions to budget holders
LLM drafts commentary from numbers and answers
Accountant edits and releases the pack
in_practice.logs_to: Pack version and commentary history on SharePoint

evidence.claim: Power BI reports refresh from scheduled extracts and support variance visuals
Copilot in Power BI can generate narrative summaries of report pages

risks: Commentary that sounds right but misstates the cause
Budget holders answer the bot less seriously than a person
research_questions: How many days after close does the pack go out today, and where is the delay?
Is the AFAS extract cost centre structure stable enough for a fixed mapping?
Do budget holders read the commentary or only the numbers?

tasks.short: Check payroll against contracts and the loonaangifte: WW premium rates, WGA/ZW risk, wage tax and agency liability.

today.trigger: Year end, an audit request, a Belastingdienst query, or a change in premium rules.
steps: Export payroll journals and employee contract data from AFAS
Check per employee whether the low WW premium is justified by a written permanent contract
Reconcile payroll journal with GL and the loonaangifte totals
Check agency invoices for G-account and chain liability (ketenaansprakelijkheid) requirements
Report differences to Payroll Specialist and Controller
drudgery: Matching contract types with premium codes for 1,200 employees by hand
Reconciling journal totals line by line
today.time_sinks: Contract-to-premium checks across many employees and many contract changes in the flex season.

lenses.faster: A script compares every employee's contract type, hours and premium code and lists only mismatches.
lenses.autonomous: After each pay run, reconciliations run on their own and mismatches go to the Payroll Specialist before the loonaangifte is filed.
lenses.ambitious: Monthly full-population checks instead of a yearly sample, avoiding back-payments of the high WW premium.
lenses.joy: No more line-by-line matching; the accountant handles the cases that need judgment.
lenses.options: For each mismatch, the possible corrections and their cost are shown.
lenses.altitude: The accountant maintains the rule set as premium and tax rules change each January.
reach: HR Administrator: contract data quality fixes

tasks.human_edge: Interpreting Dutch premium and tax rules in edge cases, and agreeing corrections with Payroll and the tax advisor.
tasks.pattern_why: Core checks are rules, but reading scanned contracts and agency documents needs an extraction step and corrections must be approved.

in_practice.trigger: Payroll run approved in AFAS, before the loonaangifte is filed.
steps: Pull payroll journal, contract and premium data from AFAS
Run rule checks (WW premium, hours, Zvw, GL reconciliation)
Extract contract facts from scanned documents where AFAS fields are empty
List mismatches with proposed correction
Accountant and Payroll Specialist approve corrections
in_practice.human_gate: Accountant and Payroll Specialist approve each correction before filing.
in_practice.logs_to: Payroll audit register in SharePoint per pay period

evidence.claim: The low WW premium requires a written permanent contract under the WAB; wrong codes lead to back-payment
evidence.source: Belastingdienst guidance on WW premium differentiation

evidence.claim: LLMs can extract contract type and hours from scanned employment contracts with review

risks: Payroll data is sensitive personal data under AVG; access and processing must be limited
Rules change yearly and an outdated rule set gives false comfort
research_questions: How many WW premium corrections were made in the last three years?
Are contract type fields in AFAS complete for all current employees?
Who is accountable for the rule set update each January?

tasks.short: Advise HR and management on cost of pay, benefits and pension choices, and on finance system setup.

today.trigger: Request from HR Director, CAO negotiation, benefit change, or a new system idea.
steps: Clarify the question with HR or management
Gather cost data from AFAS and the CAO text
Calculate options in Excel
Explain the outcome in a meeting or memo
drudgery: Rebuilding cost models from scratch for each question
Looking up CAO articles and pension rules
today.time_sinks: Building cost calculations and finding the right rules.

lenses.faster: A copilot finds the relevant CAO articles and builds a first cost model from AFAS data.
lenses.autonomous: Not suited; advice starts with a person's question.
lenses.ambitious: Every CAO or benefit proposal comes with a full cost impact per site and per year before negotiation.
lenses.joy: Less time on lookups, more on talking with HR about what the choice means for people.
lenses.options: Three to five benefit or pay scenarios with cost and effect on employee groups.
lenses.altitude: The accountant maintains a reusable personnel cost model others can query.
reach: Compensation and Benefits Specialist: cost modelling
HR Business Partner: cost questions from site management

tasks.human_edge: Trust and context: knowing the people, the OR position, and what is politically possible.
tasks.pattern_why: Advice depends on conversation and judgment; AI speeds up research and modelling.

in_practice.trigger: Advice request from HR or management.
steps: Copilot retrieves CAO articles and policy from SharePoint
Copilot builds scenario cost model from AFAS data
Accountant checks numbers and assumptions
Accountant presents advice

evidence.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot can answer questions over SharePoint documents
LLMs misquote collective agreement clauses without retrieval

risks: Wrong CAO interpretation leads to wrong advice
Individual salary data exposed in prompts
research_questions: How many advice requests come per year and how long do they take?
Are CAO texts on SharePoint current and machine-readable?
Would the Compensation and Benefits Specialist welcome a shared cost model?

tasks.short: Test new finance systems or changes, such as an AFAS module or agency invoice import, before they go live.

today.trigger: System change or new integration planned.
steps: Read the design and process description
Write test cases and expected results
Run tests with sample data
Report issues and sign off
today.time_sinks: Writing test cases and preparing test data.

lenses.faster: AI drafts test cases, control matrices and test data from the design document.
lenses.autonomous: Regression tests on journal postings run automatically after each AFAS change.
lenses.ambitious: Every system change gets a full control test, not only large projects.
lenses.joy: Less script writing; more thinking about what could go wrong.
lenses.options: Several test scenarios including edge cases a person would skip.
lenses.altitude: The accountant designs the control test library and reviews coverage.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: test support for HR-finance interfaces

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which process failures matter and deciding if a system is fit to go live.
tasks.pattern_why: Judgment on fitness stays human; AI accelerates test design and data.

steps: Copilot reads design documents and drafts test cases
Copilot generates synthetic test data
Accountant runs and reviews tests
Accountant signs off or blocks

evidence.claim: LLMs can draft test cases from functional specifications

risks: Missed edge cases if AI-generated tests are trusted blindly
Real personal data used as test data (AVG)
research_questions: How many system changes per year need finance testing?
Is there an AFAS test environment available?
Which past go-lives caused finance errors?

tasks.short: Report audit results and asset use to management and recommend operational or financial changes.

today.trigger: After audits, control reviews, or periodic asset reviews.
steps: Collect findings and asset data
Analyse impact
Draft report and recommendations
Discuss with management

lenses.faster: AI drafts the report and slides from the findings register and asset data.
lenses.autonomous: A quarterly asset utilisation report on trucks, forklifts and warehouse equipment is produced without prompting.
lenses.ambitious: Each recommendation tracked to completion with financial effect measured.
lenses.joy: Less formatting; more discussion with site managers.
lenses.options: Several recommendation sets with cost and benefit.
lenses.altitude: The accountant owns the findings register and follow-up process.

tasks.human_edge: Choosing what to recommend and persuading management.
tasks.pattern_why: The message and recommendations are the accountant's; AI drafts.

in_practice.trigger: Audit or review completed; quarterly asset report date.
steps: Pull findings register and fixed asset data
Copilot drafts report and slides
Accountant edits recommendations
Present to management

evidence.claim: Copilot in PowerPoint creates presentations from Word documents

risks: Generic recommendations that ignore site context
Asset usage data not available in AFAS
research_questions: Where is equipment usage data held today?
How many past recommendations were implemented?
What report format does management actually read?

role.altitude: From preparing analyses and checks by hand to owning the data pipelines, control rules and forecast models that run on AFAS, bank and agency data, and reviewing their exceptions.
reach: Bookkeeper: pre-payment checks and AP exceptions
FP&A Analyst: variance commentary and reforecast drafts
Controller: management pack and control documentation
role.ceiling_note: Limited by data quality in AFAS and agency portals, AVG and works council rules on monitoring, and judgment on tax and CAO interpretation; perhaps 40% of task hours can be freed, mostly in data gathering and reconciliation.
skills_to_grow: Data modelling in Power BI and SQL
Dutch payroll premium and tax rules
role.ambitious_version: The two accountants run continuous control monitoring and a rolling forecast over 100% of transactions, cutting days to close and giving the business a forecast it trusts.
